result.title: How Firm Are AI Models' Ethical Boundaries? A Pay-Stub Editing Test of 15 Models
result.comment: 11 pages: 4 pages of main content, 1 page of references, and 6 appendix pages; 7 figures and 4 tables; ancillary data and code included
result.summary: Can a small change in wording move an AI model from refusing a sensitive request to acting on it? We test 15 models on the same request to increase the income shown on a pay stub. Across 445 observable trials, models issue editing calls in 14.1% of cases when a loan purpose is stated, 33.1% when the purpose is omitted, and 66.2% when the change is described as fixing a printing error. Astra refuses all ten loan-purpose requests but issues calls in all ten purpose-omitted trials. Fable, Opus, and Muse Spark issue none across all three wordings; Sonnet issues some under the latter two. Response excerpts illustrate different ways of refusing, redirecting, or justifying an edit. The file is a marked test document and all tools are simulated. These results probe how boundaries behave in one setting; they do not prove an overall ethics ranking or that a harmful real-world edit succeeded.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用同一份工资单改数请求的三种措辞（说明贷款用途、省略用途、称作修复打印错误）测试 15 个模型的编辑调用率，并辅以拒绝与合理化回复的片段分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究关注的是措辞框架下的安全边界与拒绝行为，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的表示、证据筛选、状态更新或停止决策，也无可供核查的 latent 或训练线索，故排除。
